questions.q: Why does this capstone provision the Storage Account and Event Hub through a module instead of declaring them directly in the root configuration?
options: Modules are required for every single resource in Terraform, with no exceptions
It's an arbitrary style choice with no real reasoning behind it
They're the two resources every environment needs identically, making them a good fit for a reusable module — unlike the resource group and Fabric Capacity, declared directly
The Storage Account and Event Hub cannot be declared outside of a module
questions.explain: A module makes the most sense for a set of resources that gets reused identically across environments — exactly the landing-zone pair.

questions.q: Why is the `azurerm` remote-state backend configured before the first `apply`, rather than added later?
options: Local state is always faster and safer for a real capstone project
Terraform requires a remote backend to be configured after every apply, never before
So a second engineer picking up the same platform later has the same state available, rather than starting from local state that would need migrating
Remote state has no real benefit over local state for this project
questions.explain: Lesson 17 covered exactly this risk — local state that only exists on one machine can't be safely shared or recovered.

questions.q: What does the `terraform plan` output in this lesson actually show, before anything is created?
options: The final billing cost of the deployment
A live dashboard of resources already running in Azure
A named diff listing every resource — across both the root configuration and the module — that will be created
Nothing useful — plan output is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: The plan names each specific resource, including ones nested inside the module, before apply ever runs.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what real gap does this capstone project actually fill from earlier in the Data Engineering track?
options: It only relates to courses outside the Data Engineering track
It replaces the need for any pipeline code that was built in earlier courses
The infrastructure Career & Capstone's Project 2 and Project 3 both needed standing before any pipeline logic could run
It has no real connection to any earlier course in the track
questions.explain: Those capstone projects needed real infrastructure provisioned first — this course's own capstone provides exactly that missing piece, made real.

questions.q: What resource types does this capstone provision together, per this lesson?
options: Only Azure SQL resources
A Kubernetes cluster and a container registry
A resource group, a Storage Account, an Event Hub, and a Fabric Capacity
Only a virtual machine and a network security group
questions.explain: These are the same four resource types this course taught individually in Chapters 1-3, now provisioned together as one platform.
